html:
Ruler of the Songhai Empire from 1493 to 1528, under whom it reached its greatest size. He had been a general of Sonni Ali and took the throne from Sonni Ali's son, founding the Askia dynasty.

Where Sonni Ali had clashed with Muslim scholars, Askia Muhammad courted them. He made the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1496 to 1497 and came home with the title of caliph for the western Sahel. He brought in Islamic law, consulted jurists such as al-Maghili, and made Timbuktu a centre of learning.

He also built a state: provinces under governors, a standing army, a fleet of boats on the Niger, and standard weights and measures for trade. In 1528, old and blind, he was deposed by his son. He died in 1538 and was buried in the Tomb of Askia at Gao, a mud-brick pyramid that still stands.
sum: Ruler of the Songhai Empire from 1493 to 1528, under whom it reached its greatest size. He had been a general of Sonni Ali and took the throne from Sonni Ali's son, founding the Askia dynasty.
